executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 indicate multiple concurrent disease threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential, has generated repeated epidemiological updates from PAHO across the Americas region, representing the highest-priority biosecurity concern. Dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, and mpox are circulating simultaneously in the Americas, creating compounded vector-borne and zoonotic pressure. Additional concerns include rising pertussis activity, measles resurgence, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, and the onset of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season signaling potential novel strain emergence.
bottomLine: Concurrent circulation of BSL-3 avian influenza A(H5N1) alongside multiple epidemic-prone diseases across the Americas and Europe demands heightened surveillance, cross-border coordination, and pandemic preparedness activation.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates spanning November 2025 to March 2026 indicating sustained activity
BSL-3 select agent with documented mammalian spillover and pandemic potential
Repeated alerts from both animal and human surveillance categories suggesting zoonotic interface pressure
threats.action: Activate pandemic influenza preparedness protocols; enhance human-animal interface surveillance; coordinate with FAO and OIE on poultry outbreak containment; pre-position antiviral stockpiles and monitor for human case clusters

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating elevated transmission risk
BSL-3 select agent; vaccine-preventable but vaccination coverage gaps persist in endemic zones
Concurrent vector (Aedes/Haemagogus) activity amplified by dengue and chikungunya co-circulation
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations; strengthen entomological surveillance; ensure diagnostic laboratory capacity; issue travel health advisories for endemic areas

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 indicating ongoing transmission
Co-circulation with chikungunya and yellow fever suggests sustained Aedes aegypti vector activity
Historical seasonal pattern suggests acceleration into mid-2026 Southern Hemisphere winter transition
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations; enhance case surveillance and serotyping; prepare healthcare systems for potential surge in severe dengue cases; issue public health advisories

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update April 2026 confirming continued transmission in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent requiring enhanced biosafety measures in clinical and laboratory settings
Sustained community transmission reported following 2022-2024 global outbreak trajectory
threats.action: Maintain enhanced case detection and contact tracing; ensure vaccine availability for high-risk populations; enforce BSL-3 specimen handling protocols; monitor for clade divergence

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates within three months (December 2025 and March 2026) indicating resurgent activity
Multi-country pattern suggests waning vaccine immunity and potential vaccine-escape strains
Elevated risk to infants and immunocompromised populations
threats.action: Review and reinforce maternal and childhood immunization schedules; conduct outbreak investigations; evaluate circulating strains for vaccine antigen divergence; strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating measles resurgence
Post-COVID immunization gap has created susceptible cohorts across multiple age groups
Risk of re-endemization in previously eliminated areas
threats.action: Conduct rapid supplementary immunization activities in low-coverage areas; enhance case-based surveillance and laboratory confirmation; investigate importation chains and vaccination status of cases

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alerts in January 2026 and April 2026 flagging simultaneous influenza and RSV activity
ECDC weekly threat reports across April-May 2026 monitoring respiratory virus pressure in Europe
Southern Hemisphere season onset April 2026 signals potential new strain importation risk
threats.action: Monitor circulating strains for antigenic drift; ensure healthcare surge capacity for respiratory illness wave; promote vaccination uptake; strengthen ILI/SARI sentinel surveillance networks

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
threats.pathogen: Sin Nombre virus / Andes virus (Hantavirus spp.)
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert December 2025 indicating HPS activity in the Americas
BSL-3 pathogen with high case fatality rate; no approved antiviral treatment
Rodent reservoir activity linked to environmental and climate factors
threats.action: Enhance rodent control programs in high-risk areas; educate healthcare workers on early clinical recognition; ensure BSL-3 specimen handling; investigate cases for potential person-to-person transmission (Andes virus concern)

selectAgentSummary: Three BSL-3/BSL-4 select agents have been identified in active circulation: (1) Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — a Tier 1 BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential, subject to multiple PAHO alerts across the Americas in late 2025 and early 2026; (2) Yellow Fever virus — a BSL-3 select agent with active transmission prompting a PAHO epidemiological alert in March 2026; (3) Mpox virus (MPXV) — a BSL-3 select agent with confirmed ongoing transmission in the Americas as of April 2026. Additionally, Hantavirus (HPS) is a BSL-3 pathogen flagged in December 2025. All four require enhanced biosafety protocols, specialized laboratory handling, and immediate notification to national biosafety authorities.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR reports identified in provided surveillance titles; however, Bordetella pertussis strain monitoring warranted given resurgent activity and possible vaccine-escape variants — macrolide resistance surveillance recommended
Influenza antiviral resistance (oseltamivir) monitoring critical given H5N1 activity and expanded antiviral use in the Americas
General concern regarding empiric antibiotic overuse during respiratory virus co-circulation seasons (influenza/RSV) contributing to antimicrobial selection pressure
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen alert fatigue risk: at least 8 concurrent disease threats across the Americas may strain public health response capacity and dilute surveillance resources
Repeated H5N1 updates (November 2025, March 2026) suggest sustained or expanding geographic spread of avian influenza in the Americas, increasing pandemic risk window
Post-pandemic immunization gap driving resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) across multiple countries simultaneously
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset (April 2026) coinciding with active RSV and dengue transmission creates compounded respiratory-vector-borne burden
ECDC issuing weekly threat reports continuously across Weeks 16-20 (April-May 2026) suggests elevated and sustained multi-threat monitoring in Europe

GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (PAHO February 2026) represents an emerging pharmacovigilance signal with potential public health implications distinct from infectious disease surveillance
Co-circulation of three Aedes-transmitted viruses (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) in the Americas indicates hyperendemic vector conditions likely amplified by climate-driven range expansion
